sections.title: Stateless Web App: WhatIsTheTime.com — Scaling from Single EC2 to Multi-AZ
keyTopics: Section intro and case study roadmap
Elastic IP with single public EC2
Instance replacement breaks DNS A records
ELB with Alias record and health checks
Auto Scaling group with private instances
sections.objective: Choose the right combination of Elastic IP, Route 53 alias records, ELB, Auto Scaling groups and multi-AZ deployment to make a stateless web app horizontally scalable and highly available without downtime.

sections.title: Stateful Web App: MyClothes.com — Sessions, Caching, RDS and Security Groups
keyTopics: RDS read replicas for scaling reads
sections.objective: Design a 3-tier stateful web architecture that keeps EC2 stateless using ElastiCache or DynamoDB sessions, scales reads with replicas or caching, and restricts traffic with chained security groups.

sections.title: Stateful Web App: MyWordPress.com — Aurora, EBS vs EFS for Images
keyTopics: EBS vs EFS for distributed apps
sections.objective: Distinguish when to store uploaded content on EBS (single instance) versus EFS (shared across a multi-AZ Auto Scaling group), and explain Aurora's multi-AZ and read replica benefits.

sections.title: Instantiating Applications Quickly and the Typical 3-Tier Web App
keyTopics: Golden AMI plus User Data hybrid
sections.objective: Select the fastest way to instantiate EC2, RDS and EBS resources (Golden AMI, User Data, snapshots) and describe the standard 3-tier architecture with public, private and data subnets.

sections.title: Elastic Beanstalk — Overview, Components, Platforms and Deployment Modes
keyTopics: Web server tier vs worker tier
Single instance vs HA deployment mode
sections.objective: Explain what Elastic Beanstalk manages versus what the developer owns, and distinguish web server tier, worker tier, and single instance versus load-balanced deployment modes.

notes: Exam focus: Task 2.1 (scalable web architectures) and Task 2.2 (removing single points of failure). Recurring scenario pattern: pick the layer that fixes the stated constraint — DNS A record + fixed IPs cannot survive instance replacement (use ELB alias + ASG); sticky sessions pin users to an instance (prefer externalized session store); cookies are limited to 4KB and can be altered (validate, or use session_id); EBS is AZ-bound single-instance (use EFS for shared uploads). Distractors often swap read replicas for multi-AZ (replicas scale reads, multi-AZ is failover) or DynamoDB for ElastiCache sessions. Beanstalk: free service, you pay for EC2/ELB/RDS underneath; only application code is the developer's responsibility; worker tier scales on SQS message depth. Background: stickiness is configured on the load balancer, not the ASG.
